notes:
Background: Hummingbird runs an RTB stack for display & video ads. Request profile: very short prompts (10-50 tokens), heavy fanout (100-1k reqs/ms bursts during peak auctions), typical sustained traffic ~10M calls/day but huge spikes. P50 target currently 8-12ms, absolute requirement: p99 <= 50ms for bidding decision path. Cost sensitive: wants to reduce per-request token cost and avoid overprovisioning GPUs. Prefer open models but will consider Redwood-verified variants.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-09-12: Intro call (AE Aisha). high level requirements captured. Fireflies: ff_20251015_7382.
- 2025-09-25: Architecture deep-dive with infra/ML (SE Marco). Collected sample traffic traces + tail-latency stats.
- 2025-10-03: Security questionnaire submitted (drive:/security/hummingbird-security-faq.md). Waiting answers on KMS + audit log retention.
- 2025-10-15: Demo of hosted API latency baseline (recorded ff_20251015_7382). P50 15ms on small model, p99 ~120ms with cold KV caches.
- 2025-10-28: Follow-up: discussed batching, prefix caching, and quantization tradeoffs (ff_20251028_7491).
- 2025-10-29: Redwood asked for production-like perf test plan; Hummingbird agreed to provide traffic replay + sample prompt set.

Use-case & reqs (TL;DR):
- Workload: Real-time bidding + reranking micro-decisions + short-turn assistant for internal ops.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 12ms, p95 < 25ms, p99 <= 50ms for bidding path. Tail latency critical.
- Throughput: baseline 8k QPS sustained in test; bursty peaks 80k QPS for <2 minutes.
- Accuracy: reranking delta must be within 1.5% of current model; cannot lose top-3 quality.
- Cost sensitivity: target <$0.0015 per inference on average. Need clear unit economics for batching vs. dedicated pools.
- Model preference: open-source 7B-13B family (quantized int8/int4 considered), Redwood-verified low-latency variants.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants under load; prefer region routing (NA primary, EU secondary).

POC asks (what they want Redwood to run):
- Perf benchmark suite using their replayed traffic (attached). Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, effective cost per request across configs.
- Experiments: adaptive batching window + continuous batching, prefix/KV caching (warm vs cold), int8 vs int4 quantized runs, CPU vs GPU inference cost comparison.
- Failure modes: simulated node loss to test graceful degradation & model fallback.
- Deliverables: perf report + recommended batching/cache/quant settings and expected unit cost delta.

Quotes/snippets: "If p99 goes above 50ms we lose auctions — real revenue impact" — J. Kim (CTO).
"we need a repeatable benchmark that mirrors our spikes; synthetic steady-state numbers are useless" — Head of Infra.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to schedule 3-day perf POC (week of 2025-11-10).
- Hummingbird to provide traffic replay + sample prompt set by 2025-11-05.
- Legal to start PCI/GDPR scoping; security team to answer KMS/audit questions by 2025-11-07.

Notes for AE/SE: Stick to production-like traffic for tests (burst characteristics, cold cache scenarios). Focus POC on batching latency tradeoff graphs and quantization accuracy matrices. Prepare cost model spreadsheet mapping batch size and KV hit rate to $/inference. Make explicit fallbacks for model variant routing in the playbook.
